A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SASSHA with matching authors, algorithms and core experiments. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original optimization, sharpness, image-classification, language-modeling, label-noise and timing experiments in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical studies and adds GPT2-small pretraining results in Appendix J, Table 17.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same normalized perturbation, gradient momentum, absolute-value and square-root Hessian stabilization, lazy updates and weight decay. M-SASSHA and G-SASSHA already appear in v1. The expanded explanations and theoretical analysis do not establish an implemented method change.

E1.justification: v2 Appendix J adds language pretraining on a corpus reported as OpenWebText. CIFAR-10/100, ImageNet, Wikitext-2, GLUE and the existing label-noise scenarios are retained. This extends corpus coverage within an existing task.

E2.justification: The new GPT2 comparison evaluates Sophia-G and Sophia-G with SAM, neither evaluated in v1, alongside AdamW and SAM-AdamW. Existing Sophia-H, AdaHessian, Shampoo, first-order and advanced SAM comparisons remain.

E3.justification: Appendix J introduces GPT2-small training for 50,000 iterations, specifies rho = 0.1 for SAM-related methods and adopts cited best configurations for AdamW and Sophia-G. Existing experiments retain their reported budgets, schedules and hyperparameter searches.

E4.justification: The square-root, absolute-value, lazy-Hessian, label-noise, extended-budget and Sophia-H-with-SAM analyses retain their experimental evidence. Appendix renumbering and expanded explanations do not add ablations; the GPT2 addition is a benchmark comparison.

E5.justification: Table 3 newly reports SAM-AdamW pretraining perplexity as 158.06±0.23. The other uncertainty values added there already appeared in v1 Table 7. Appendix J explicitly discloses a single seed for GPT2 experiments; no increase in existing run counts is established.

E6.justification: New Table 17 reports GPT2 perplexity of 19.015 for SASSHA, behind Sophia-G (18.751) and Sophia-G with SAM (18.773), but ahead of AdamW (19.353) and SAM-AdamW (19.196). Table 7 revises SAM's WRN-28-10/CIFAR-100 accuracy from 82.56±0.13 to 83.14±0.13, matching Table 2. Other retained results are substantively unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 adds Section 4.6 and Appendix D: fixed-point and linear-stability definitions, Corollary 4.6 bounding sharpness and stochastic-Hessian moments, and Theorem D.5 with a proof. This substantially expands the theoretical treatment beyond the retained convex convergence analysis in Section 4.5 and Appendix C.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same contributions concerning sharpness, stable Hessian approximation, generalization and efficiency. The conclusion makes lazy-update and label-noise benefits more explicit, but these claims were already present in v1.

C2.justification: Section 4.6 adds a stability-based explanation involving flatness and Hessian uniformity. Section 4.2 replaces the Newton-optimal-rescaling assertion with an explanation about gradient direction and Hessian magnitudes, while related appendices expand the clipping rationale. The conclusion specifies missing convergence-rate, generalization-bound and implicit-bias guarantees.

D1.justification: Appendix J documents the new GPT2 model, iteration budget, perturbation radius and source of baseline configurations. Existing implementation descriptions, search grids and code-access information are retained; no new implementation or resource release is established.

R1.justification: v2 adds Wu et al. (2018) for the stability perspective and Gao et al. (2020) with the new language experiment. It removes four references accompanying the Newton-rescaling discussion. Section 2 and the overall positioning remain stable; the Shin et al. publication update concerns the same work.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites expand Section 4.2, Appendices B/F/I and the conclusion; Section 5.3 changes paragraph order. v2 inserts a flatness subsection, two appendices and an impact statement, while retaining most existing prose and the overall narrative structure.

P2.justification: v2 adds the GPT2 results table, adjusts table widths, spacing and row order, and relocates existing displays through reflow. Table 7 relabels worst-case sharpness as gradient-direction sharpness, consistent with Section 3. The seven existing figures retain their substantive plots.

improvement.justification: The added GPT2 benchmark and reporting corrections improve coverage and consistency. However, the major theoretical addition has unresolved internal problems: Appendix D Equation (13) uses an unnormalized perturbation unlike Algorithm 1, and Theorem D.5 states a sufficient stability condition whereas Corollary 4.6 claims necessary conditions. These issues weaken the new mechanism explanation. Given these harms alongside limited empirical gains from a single-seed experiment, the net quality direction is uncertain.
